html:
On 8 December 2024 rebel forces entered Damascus and President Bashar al-Assad fled to Russia, ending more than half a century of rule by the Assad family. It came after an offensive of only eleven days.

The offensive was led by Hayat Tahrir al-Sham, an Islamist group based in Idlib, under Ahmed al-Sharaa. Assad's army, worn out and unpaid after the civil war, collapsed. His allies were weakened: Russia was busy in Ukraine and Hezbollah had been battered by Israel. Aleppo fell in days, then Hama, Homs and Damascus.

Crowds opened the prisons, such as Saydnaya. Al-Sharaa became the interim president. Millions of refugees began to weigh going home. See also Hafez al-Assad.
sum: On 8 December 2024 rebel forces entered Damascus and President Bashar al-Assad fled to Russia, ending more than half a century of rule by the Assad family. It came after an offensive of only eleven days.
